top_strength: The best moment was an unprompted objection save. When the customer explained her schedule made a walkthrough impossible — 'I work today and tomorrow and I start work late and I finished late. You guys close at five, I close at eight' — Danah immediately came back with 'But actually, we can do it on the weekends too, we can do the virtual walkthrough. Yup, we are open on the weekends,' and then gave the exact Saturday hours (9:00 AM to 4:30 PM). That turned a dead end into a Saturday plan. Her core pricing block was also clean and confident: $192 for two movers Sunday through Thursday, $96 per additional mover, gas/truck/taxes/insurance/wrap included, disassembly and reassembly included, and a clearly explained $140 flat trip fee per truck because the address sits outside the free service zone.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: you cannot end a call with a customer you have no way to reach. She had already submitted a quote request, told you she was calling on a work break, and you still hung up with no name, no email and no walkthrough on the calendar. When she said 'my break is almost over,' the move was to close the loop in one line: 'Totally understand — give me just your email and I'll have the Saturday walkthrough invite and the pricing waiting for you, that's ten seconds.' Second priority: once you decide to quote the hourly rate, you own the clock. She asked you point-blank how many hours it would take. 'We won't know until the walkthrough' is only half an answer — follow it with 'What I can tell you now is the clock starts when we arrive and open the contract, there's a two-and-a-half hour minimum, and after that we bill in fifteen-minute increments, so you only pay for the time we actually use. Does that make sense?' Third, you pitched pricing without a single differentiator — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee are what make $192 an hour feel like a bargain instead of a number, and they cost you fifteen seconds. BUSINESS RISK: the customer said '2100 no... 4100' and you recorded 2100 without resolving it. A 4100 sqft home routed and crewed as 2100 is exactly the estimate-accuracy failure we are trying to close — the walkthrough will catch it, but only if the walkthrough actually happens, and it is not booked. NOTE ON GRADING: this was classified as a walkthrough_scheduler (2100+ sqft correctly routed to a virtual walkthrough), so Estimate and Save Your Ass were granted as N/A. Pricing and Clock were graded rather than N/A'd because she chose to deliver a full hourly-rate pitch on this call, which puts both sections in play.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and clear but almost entirely mechanical — dozens of 'Mm-hmm' and 'Okay' fillers, zero use of the customer's name, no empathy statement anywhere despite the customer audibly struggling to be understood and rushing on a work break; the weekend-availability save was the one moment of genuine responsiveness.
